goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:29 — Referer header is attacker-controlled and only its host is checked against embeddable_host, so any site can spoof it to trigger retrieve_topic jobs / SSRF-style fetches against the embeddable host for arbitrary paths

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` authorizes the request based on `request.referer` host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The Referer header is client-controlled and can be trivially spoofed in a direct HTTP request, so this check does not actually ensure the caller is coming from the embedding site. When `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, `best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)`. The job ultimately calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` which does `open(url).read` (HTTP fetch) and imports the fetched HTML into a topic. While `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` limits the fetch to URLs whose host equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, an attacker can still trigger server-side fetches for arbitrary paths on that host (and repeated requests by varying the path), so the finding about spoofable referer enabling job-triggered fetches is verifiably present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — import_remote(user, t[:link]) passes attacker/import-file-controlled link straight into Kernel#open via TopicEmbed.import_remote/open(url) before any URL-scheme validation, enabling classic Ruby `|command` open() command injection since only TopicEmbed.import (called after the open) validates the http(s) prefix

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` (around the shown change near line 143). In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code immediately does `open(url).read` to fetch the remote page, with no prior validation that `url` is an `http(s)` URL. The only `http(s)` check (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`) is in `TopicEmbed.import`, which is called *after* `open(url).read` has already executed. In Ruby, `Kernel#open` supports the `|cmd` form (e.g., `open('|id')`) which executes a subprocess, so passing an import-file-controlled `t[:link]` can lead to command execution before any scheme/prefix validation occurs. This is directly verifiable from the added/modified code paths in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:24 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute is applied unconditionally, so the transient 'loading' response (which self-reloads via JS) can be cached for a minute even though the topic may already be available on next request

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is called after the `if/else` that either builds `@topic_view` or `render 'loading'`, so it applies to both responses. The `loading.html.erb` view triggers `document.location.reload()` after 30 seconds, but if the loading response is cacheable for up to 60 seconds, a client/intermediate cache can serve the cached loading page on the next request even if the topic/embed is now available, delaying the transition to the real content. This caching behavior is introduced unconditionally by the diff and is a correctness/UX defect for the transient loading state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:105 — TopicEmbed.import does a check-then-create on embed_url (unique-indexed) without rescuing a uniqueness violation, so concurrent imports of the same URL (e.g. poll_feed + topic_retriever racing) can raise an unhandled RecordNotUnique instead of gracefully reusing the existing embed

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, if blank, proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so concurrent callers importing the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race to `create!`, causing an unhandled uniqueness violation (`RecordNotUnique` / `RecordInvalid`). There is no rescue/retry/“find-or-create” handling. The diff also introduces multiple potential concurrent import paths (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` calling `TopicEmbed.import` and `TopicRetriever`/`RetrieveTopic` calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `import`), and `TopicRetriever`’s `exists?` pre-check is also non-atomic, so the race is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — force: true` added to create_table for top_topics silently drops any existing table/data with no backfill or rollback path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` would drop an existing `top_topics` table if it were present when this migration runs, in normal Rails migration flow this migration is intended to be executed only once on databases where the table does not yet exist. Databases that already have the table would also already have this migration marked as run in `schema_migrations`, so the changed code would not execute and would not drop data. Therefore the finding relies on an atypical scenario (table exists but migration not recorded) rather than a clear, verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:33 — TopicRetriever (a lib class) directly instantiates and executes Jobs::PollFeed, coupling a plain retrieval library to the job-queue layer instead of enqueuing or injecting the dependency

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly (synchronously) instead of enqueuing, so the coupling described is factually present. However, this is an architectural/design critique rather than a clear defect: nothing in the diff demonstrates that calling a `Jobs::Scheduled` job’s `execute` method directly is incorrect or unsafe in this codebase, and it appears intentionally done to reuse the polling logic as part of retrieval. The finding does not identify a verifiable bug/security/correctness issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:28 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no read/open timeout so a slow/hanging feed server can block the scheduled job indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with open-uri and does not pass explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options. However, the finding claims it can block “indefinitely,” which is not verifiable from the diff: open-uri uses Net::HTTP, which has built-in default timeouts in typical Ruby versions (e.g., 60s open/read), so it’s not clearly an unbounded hang introduced by this change. At most, it’s a robustness suggestion to set explicit timeouts, not a definite defect demonstrated by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:15 — execute() has no rescue around TopicRetriever#retrieve; any exception from the HTTP fetch will fail the job with default Sidekiq retry semantics, potentially hammering the external embed host repeatedly

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, `execute` directly calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` with no `rescue` and no `sidekiq_options retry: false`. `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` ultimately calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` and HTML parsing and can raise network/HTTP exceptions. Those exceptions will bubble up and fail the job, triggering Sidekiq’s default retry behavior (since not overridden here), resulting in repeated attempts over time. While `TopicRetriever` has a 60s Redis throttle, retries occurring after the throttle window can still re-attempt the external fetch repeatedly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:39 — import_remote fetches arbitrary embed_url via open-uri with no scheme/host allowlist beyond caller checks, enabling SSRF (e.g. internal network requests, redirect-based bypass)

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` on the provided `url` with no validation/allowlist inside the method. While `TopicRetriever` performs a host equality check before calling it, `import_remote` is also called directly from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`) with no host/scheme restriction at all. Additionally, even when called via `TopicRetriever`, the check only compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and does not prevent open-uri from following redirects to other hosts/IPs, enabling redirect-based SSRF to internal resources. This is a concrete, diff-visible security issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Access control relies on comparing request.referer host to embeddable_host, but Referer is a client-supplied header that non-browser clients can freely spoof, making this an unreliable security boundary

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` enforces embedding authorization solely by checking `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and rejecting otherwise. Since `Referer` is a client-supplied header, any non-browser client (or proxy) can spoof it to bypass this gate and retrieve the embed content, so this is not a reliable access-control boundary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:26 — poll_feed fetches SiteSetting.feed_polling_url via open-uri with no scheme restriction; if the setting is ever attacker-influenced (e.g. via compromised admin session or SSRF chaining) this becomes a fetch primitive
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that PollFeed uses open-uri to fetch SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without validating/restricting it, enabling an SSRF-style arbitrary URL fetch if the setting can be attacker-controlled or influenced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:1 — poll_feed_spec only tests the guard-clause dispatch to poll_feed and never exercises the actual RSS parsing/import logic (item.link vs item.id fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML, TopicEmbed.import call) added in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add non-trivial logic in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb#poll_feed` (SimpleRSS parsing, `item.link`/`item.id` fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML`, `TopicEmbed.import`). The proposed finding correctly observes that the new spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only asserts the guard conditions and that `execute` dispatches to `poll_feed`, and it does not exercise the parsing/import behavior. However, this is a test coverage critique rather than a verifiable defect/bug/security/correctness problem introduced by the diff. The code can still be correct even if the spec is minimal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:34 — The "no previous embed" test mocks TopicRetriever.new/retrieve entirely, but the controller code enqueues a job (Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)); the test never verifies the actual embed_url/user_id args passed to the job are correct, only that some later TopicRetriever instance responds to retrieve

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`; it does not instantiate or call `TopicRetriever` directly. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`'s "no previous embed" example sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve` instead of asserting that the job is enqueued with the correct `embed_url`/`user_id`. This means the test is not actually verifying the controller’s behavior (and may fail depending on whether enqueued jobs run inline in the test env).
